story: As an operator, I want configuration loaded from environment variables so secrets stay outside the repository.
expected: DATABASE_URL is required; optional credentials default empty; numeric limits reject invalid values.

story: As an operator, I want migrations to be safely repeatable so deployment restarts do not damage the database.
expected: Each numbered migration applies once and subsequent migrate runs succeed without repeating DDL.

story: As an operator, I want configuration seeds to update existing rows without duplicates.
expected: Running migrate and seed twice retains one title, server, and source row per unique key.

story: As an operator, I want concise command help so I can discover every supported workflow.
expected: Root help lists migrate, collect, report, pulse, and replay with useful descriptions.

story: As an operator, I want to run one collector independently for debugging and backfill.
expected: collect accepts discord, twitch, kick, or press and invokes only the selected source.

story: As an operator, I want one command to run all scheduled sources while containing failures.
expected: collect all attempts all four sources in order, reports all failures, and exits nonzero if any source fails.

story: As an operator, I want missing Twitch or Kick credentials explained before collection.
expected: Missing platform credentials produce a specific nonzero error without exposing secret values.

story: As an analyst, I want weekly reports anchored to Monday so comparison windows are consistent.
expected: report accepts Monday ISO dates and rejects non-Monday dates with a clear message.

story: As an analyst, I want pulse source input validated so an accidental empty or unknown request cannot create a misleading brief.
expected: pulse rejects empty and unknown source lists and removes duplicate source names while preserving order.

story: As an analyst, I want a valid lookback window for fresh press signals.
expected: pulse accepts positive press-hour values and rejects zero or negative values.

story: As an operator, I want every external request bounded so a source cannot hang a run forever.
expected: The shared async client always uses an explicit positive timeout.

story: As a source owner, I want requests spaced so the collector behaves responsibly.
expected: The shared client enforces a minimum interval; Discord uses at least one second.

story: As an operator, I want transient failures retried without infinite loops.
expected: 429 and transient 5xx responses retry exponentially, honor Retry-After, and stop at the configured limit.

story: As a data engineer, I want every response persisted before parsing so parser changes can be audited.
expected: Response evidence is committed through a separate connection before response JSON or feed parsing occurs.

story: As a security owner, I want raw evidence free of credentials.
expected: Sensitive URL parameters, headers, and nested OAuth response fields are redacted.

story: As a data engineer, I want hashes and parser versions so evidence and transformations are traceable.
expected: Raw rows include body hash, payload kind, received time, response status, and parser version.

story: As an operator, I want run status to distinguish complete data from partial or absent data.
expected: Zero failures is success, mixed item outcomes is partial, and no successful items or fatal exceptions is failed.

story: As an operator, I want fatal failures visible to cron and deployment systems.
expected: Fatal exceptions persist a failed run and propagate to a nonzero CLI exit.

story: As an analyst, I want urgent research collections excluded from weekly benchmarks.
expected: Runs are tagged scheduled or on_demand; weekly rollups use scheduled observations only.

story: As an analyst, I want public community size and online presence without Discord authentication.
expected: Active invite codes are resolved with counts and produce snapshots containing member and presence counts.

story: As an analyst, I want widget presence used when available without making it required.
expected: A successful widget count overrides approximate presence; widget failure retains the invite snapshot.

story: As an operator, I want dead invites disabled without losing history.
expected: A 404 marks invite_dead, stores no new snapshot, preserves old rows, and does not crash the collector.

story: As an operator, I want one server failure to leave successful server snapshots intact.
expected: Network loss after progress yields partial with error detail and committed successful snapshots.

story: As an operator, I want Twitch application authentication refreshed automatically.
expected: Client credentials obtain a token; a 401 refreshes once and retries the page.

story: As an analyst, I want the first 1,000 live streams aggregated across ten pages.
expected: Cursor pagination stops at exhaustion or configured page limit and passes the next cursor correctly.

story: As an analyst, I want category viewer totals, channel counts, and the top channel.
expected: Streams are deduplicated by ID, null viewers count as zero, and aggregates use consistent semantics.

story: As an analyst, I want Twitch directory rank stored separately from sampled viewer totals.
expected: Top-games results map game IDs to one-based directory ranks in category snapshots.

story: As an operator, I want Kick auth sent to the identity host and data requests to the API host.
expected: Tokens use id.kick.com and livestreams use api.kick.com/public/v2.

story: As an analyst, I want active Kick streams collected across v2 cursor pages.
expected: The collector requests up to 1,000 rows per page and follows next_cursor until exhaustion or limit.

story: As an analyst, I want malformed or privacy-limited stream fields handled without losing valid categories.
expected: Missing categories are skipped, null viewer counts become zero, duplicate IDs are removed, and valid categories are aggregated.

story: As an operator, I want feed URLs discovered without article-page scraping.
expected: Homepage alternate links are tried first, then approved fallback paths; usable feeds are persisted.

story: As an operator, I want unresolved outlets marked unavailable while other feeds continue.
expected: A source with no usable feed records unavailable and error detail without aborting the run.

story: As an analyst, I want repeated feed items stored once despite tracking parameters.
expected: Host case, query parameters, fragment, and trailing slash differences normalize to one SHA-256 URL hash.

story: As an analyst, I want articles deterministically matched to configured aliases while retaining unmatched coverage.
expected: Case-insensitive bounded aliases assign title_slug; unmatched articles remain with null title_slug.

story: As an analyst, I want meme signals separated from press volume.
expected: Meme-class sources appear only in Meme and trend watch, not news counts.

story: As an operator, I want an active outlet feed rediscovered when its stored URL stops working.
expected: A failed stored feed triggers one fresh homepage discovery using configured homepage data before the source is marked unavailable.

story: As a reader, I want movement withheld when collection coverage is weak.
expected: Each source needs at least five complete scheduled days in both weeks; otherwise state is INSUFFICIENT DATA.

story: As a reader, I want cold-start and zero-baseline cases described correctly.
expected: Reports distinguish BASELINE, NEW, DROPPED, UP, DOWN, UNCHANGED, and INSUFFICIENT DATA.

story: As a reader, I want all platform categories for one game combined before comparison.
expected: Categories sum per title, platform, and run before weekly means, with blanks instead of zeros for absent platforms.

story: As a reader, I want movers backed by two different source classes.
expected: Multiple Discord servers or categories cannot count twice; at most Discord, Twitch, Kick, and Press contribute once each.

story: As a reader, I want one durable Markdown report and a readable HTML rendering.
expected: Both files use ISO week naming, contain seven ordered sections, and record report_runs coverage metadata.

story: As a reader, I want explicit units and comparison baselines without unsupported adjectives.
expected: Mover sentences name source-specific units, absolute change, current value, and week-over-week percentage.

story: As a reader, I want generated output free of forbidden punctuation and structurally readable.
expected: No em dash appears; HTML uses table headers, list elements, escaped text, and working links.

story: As a reader, I want counts rendered with correct singular and plural units.
expected: A value of one uses article, viewer, member, channel, or outlet; all other values use plural forms.

story: As an analyst under deadline, I want selected sources refreshed immediately.
expected: pulse runs only unique requested sources under on_demand mode and writes a timestamped brief.

story: As an analyst, I want the brief to show observations from this pulse rather than stale or scheduled runs.
expected: Discord and streaming queries are restricted to run IDs created by the current pulse.

story: As an analyst, I want available signals even when one source fails.
expected: The brief is written with collector statuses, then the command exits nonzero and lists failed sources.

story: As a data engineer, I want one stored payload reparsed without recollection.
expected: replay --response-id parses offline, records normalized JSON and parsed status, and reports the ID.

story: As a data engineer, I want every raw response from a run reparsed in order.
expected: replay --run-id processes all response IDs, reports each failure, and rejects runs with no raw responses.

story: As a compliance owner, I want browser and Discord collection limited to explicit, authorized access.
expected: Code never extracts user tokens, cookies, passwords, or hidden content; never bypasses access controls; bot collection requires permission; browser scanning is user-triggered, visible-only, bounded, and approval-gated.

story: As a compliance owner, I want committed configuration free of live credentials.
expected: .env is ignored, credential fields in .env.example are empty, and tracked source contains no live tokens, passwords, or client secrets.

story: As an operator, I want exact UTC cron examples for daily collectors and Monday reports.
expected: README documents fixed-hour independent collection and Monday report commands.
